intuition.title: Hydrothermal precursor and postannealed oxide
intuition.text: Hydrothermal processing first produces orthorhombic InOOH. Annealing at 500 °C for 1 h in normal atmosphere gives rhombohedral In2O3. Separate records preserve the intermediate and final phases with explicit parent-record lineage; these are stages of two vessel routes, not four unrelated physical batches.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental synthesis; Figure 1 and second-vessel comparison

intuition.title: Two vessels with different reported detail
intuition.text: The first experiment uses a stirred 300 mL stainless-steel pressure vessel, 0.7 M aqueous indium nitrate monohydrate, 200 °C and 4 h. The second uses a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave without stirring. The source calls its filtration, washing and drying similar to the first case; its hydrothermal concentration, temperature and dwell are not independently restated. Vessel capacities do not establish liquid charges.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental synthesis paragraph

intuition.title: Reference cells are not specimen refinements
intuition.text: For orthorhombic InOOH, cited reference values are a = 5.260 Å, b = 4.560 Å and c = 3.270 Å; the first hydrothermal specimen refines to 5.262, 4.591 and 3.258 Å. For rhombohedral In2O3, reference a = 5.487 Å and c = 14.510 Å differ from the first annealed specimen values 5.469 and 14.491 Å. Only the refined specimen values enter product measurements. No atomic coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, XRD phase indexing and lattice refinements

intuition.title: XRD sizes and TEM have distinct evidence
intuition.text: The annealed stainless-steel route has a Scherrer mean of 12 nm and reported range 10–18 nm. The continuing XRD comparison gives a mean of 22 nm and range 19–26 nm for the annealed Teflon-lined route. These are author-reported size estimates, not newly counted TEM distributions. Figure 2a qualitatively confirms nanometer particles only for the stainless-steel route; its 100 nm scale bar is not a particle diameter.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Scherrer estimate, second-vessel comparison and Figure 2

intuition.title: Stirring is an interpretation, not an isolated causal test
intuition.text: The authors attribute the size difference to stirring effects. The experiments also use different vessel capacities and liner materials, and not every second-experiment condition is restated. The attribution is retained as the authors’ interpretation without treating it as a controlled one-variable law.

intuition.title: Phase evidence and application motivation
intuition.text: Figure 1b indexes rhombohedral In2O3, R-3c (167), ASTM 22-336. The authors report no detectable XRD peaks from other indium compounds; this does not establish an absolute chemical-purity limit. Figure 2b supports rhombohedral diffraction for the first annealed specimen. Introductory conductivity and sensing claims refer to background literature, not measurements on these powders.

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
